title: Sell Mineral Rights in Kansas
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Kansas | Royalty Buyer USA
metaDescription: Heirs of a Kansas mineral interest in the Hugoton field or Mississippian Lime? We untangle split ownership and buy your share. Free, honest offer.
heroLead: More than almost any state we work in, Kansas mineral ownership comes to us in pieces — heirs, half-interests, and deeds that were never quite finished being sorted out.
intro: We've sat with enough families going through this ourselves to recognize the pattern the moment a Kansas call comes in: grandpa or grandma owned the minerals under the home place, they passed, the land maybe sold to a neighbor at some point but the minerals didn't go with it, and now three or four siblings or cousins each hold a fraction of a fraction, with statements arriving under names that don't quite match anymore. Kansas has two big legacy plays behind most of this ownership — the Hugoton field in the southwest, one of the largest natural gas fields in the country, and the Mississippian Lime trend across south-central Kansas, an oil and gas play that saw a real drilling boom in the early 2010s and has settled into steadier production since.

We buy Kansas royalty and mineral interests in both, and we're comfortable working through the ownership tangles that come with them. If you're one of several heirs trying to figure out who owns what percentage of a Hugoton or Mississippian Lime interest, that's exactly the kind of situation we handle every week.

sections.heading: Split estates and the heir problem
paragraphs: In Kansas, it's extremely common for the surface and the minerals to have gone separate ways generations ago, so the family farming the land today may have nothing to do with who owns the minerals underneath it. Layer in unfinished probates, where mineral interests were never formally transferred out of a deceased owner's name, and you end up with statements addressed to people who died decades ago, checks that go uncashed, or interests split so many ways that no single heir holds more than a tiny fraction.

This is normal for Kansas, not a red flag on your family's paperwork. We start by helping you understand exactly what percentage you actually hold and what would need to happen, sometimes a simple affidavit of heirship, sometimes a probate, to clean up title enough to transfer it. We're not attorneys, so for anything requiring court filings we'll point you to one, but we can usually tell you which situation you're in before you spend money finding out.

sections.heading: The Hugoton field: old, huge, and steady
paragraphs: The Hugoton field has been producing natural gas since the 1920s and remains one of the largest gas fields ever discovered in the U.S., spanning Kansas, Oklahoma, and Texas. Wells here decline slowly compared to a modern shale play, and a lot of southwest Kansas royalty owners have held interests that have paid modest, relatively stable amounts for decades rather than spiking and crashing.

Because Hugoton is so mature, new drilling is rare, and value comes almost entirely from what's already producing and how many years of life remain. We price Hugoton interests against long production histories that are well documented, which actually makes these easier to value confidently than a newer, less-proven play.

sections.heading: The Mississippian Lime: a boom that settled down
paragraphs: The Mississippian Lime saw heavy horizontal drilling activity roughly between 2010 and 2015 across counties like Barber, Comanche, and Harper, and while activity has slowed considerably since then, a lot of those wells are still producing today. If your family leased during that boom, your royalty check has likely settled into a lower, more predictable range than it was during the initial flush production years, which is the normal decline pattern for this kind of well.

We look at where your specific well sits on that curve, whether it's still in early decline or has leveled off, and price the interest accordingly rather than assuming every Mississippian Lime well behaves the same way.

sections.heading: Getting a fractured Kansas interest ready to sell
paragraphs: If you're one of several heirs, you don't need everyone to agree before you find out what your own share is worth — we can quote an individual heir's fractional interest and let each family member decide separately. If title needs cleanup first, we'll tell you plainly rather than making a quiet assumption, and we'll work on a timeline that accounts for that.

Once title is clear and you accept an offer, closing runs through a title company or attorney escrow like any other state, typically within a few weeks. There's no cost to find out what your share is worth, even if it turns out the honest answer is that title needs sorting out first.

faqs.question: Your grandmother's mineral interest was never formally transferred after she passed. Can you still buy it?
faqs.answer: We can usually still make an offer, but title typically needs to be cleared first through an heirship affidavit or probate before a sale can close. We'll tell you which applies to your situation.

faqs.question: If you only own a small fraction split among several cousins. Do you have to get everyone to agree to sell?
faqs.answer: No. We can quote and purchase an individual heir's fractional share separately; other family members can decide on their own whether to sell.

faqs.question: Is Hugoton field gas royalty still worth anything after 100 years of production?
faqs.answer: Often yes, since Hugoton wells decline slowly and have long, well-documented production histories that let us price remaining value with confidence.

faqs.question: Your Mississippian Lime royalty has dropped a lot since it was first leased. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: Yes, this is typical decline behavior for wells drilled during the 2010-2015 boom in that play. We price your interest based on where it currently sits on that curve, not the peak production years.

faqs.question: How do you even find out what percentage you own in a Kansas interest?
faqs.answer: Send us whatever documentation you have, even partial or outdated statements, and we'll help research the current ownership picture before quoting a number.
